significance.justification: A verified-true result would establish a form-(iii) behavioral law—across several conceptual mappings, performance follows “CONGRUENT > NEUTRAL > INCONGRUENT,” incongruent errors favor the “metaphor-default answer,” and neutral restatement reverses much of the loss—plus a causal claim that metaphorical framing scaffolds the named reasoning behaviors. This fixes predictions across numeric, temporal, evaluative, and quantity tasks and bears directly on the formal-versus-functional competence distinction discussed by Mahowald et al. (2024, “Dissociating language and thought in large language models”), although attention or trace correlations would not by themselves establish the detailed internal mechanism. True and false are distinguishable: a robust pattern would establish both a phenomenon and a behavior-level mechanism, whereas a null would rule out the proposed generalized congruency law and dependence on these mappings, though not prove metaphor-independent reasoning universally. Topic substitution fails: the broad topic “relationship between language and AI intelligence” alone would not license the claim’s specific cross-metaphor ordering, directional-error signature, or neutralization prediction, so the score reflects the claim rather than the topic.

reach.justification: The claim hands over two named handles: the measurable “congruency effect (congruent minus incongruent accuracy)” with its “directional-error bias rate,” and the intervention “explicitly restate the problem in metaphor-neutral form before solving.” The latter is ex ante because it can be applied before an answer is produced, giving benchmark designers, auditors, and model users an action window rather than merely explaining errors post hoc. The asserted ordering spans four metaphor classes and multiple model families, and as a relation it predicts what should recur after quantities are re-estimated on another model, although its stated anchoring to “English-dominant mappings” limits cross-linguistic transfer. Topic substitution fails: the generic language–intelligence topic supplies neither this diagnostic nor the neutralization intervention, so the above-median reach comes from the claim-specific handles and transferable relation.
